scope: v0.2 task adapters (8 bundles), weight-only MatMul quantization, FP32 activations
gate: scripts/verify-quantized.ts + browser-tasks.ts quantized: token ids, offsets, positions and decoded spans/box/point must match the FP32 fixtures exactly; span score / box confidence drift <= 0.02 (v0.1 quantization tolerance); raw logit deviation reported only

q8.config: per-output-channel signed INT8 + DequantizeLinear, opset 17, external data preserved

ner.note: until 2026-11-12 the data file held its weights twice (1150 MB): a second quantizer run into the folder appended them (python/quantize_tasks.py, fixed); the trimmed file holds the same tensors

vision-box.note: encoder-only: the task graph stays FP32 because any quantization of it flips the point argmax (knife-edge); quantized with --only vision; until 2026-11-12 the image-encoder data file held its weights twice (859 MB), trimmed like ner

config.text (evidence, relation, span, span_set: python/quantize_gptq.py: GPTQ INT4, asymmetric groups of 32 with fp16 scales, as MatMulNBits; the token table (INT4 groups of 32) and the 24 backbone layers are one shared file (backbone/fast/q4/backbone.onnx.data); each bundle keeps its own LoRA (INT8 per channel), layers 20 to 23 (INT4) and heads; export report reports/quantization-gptq.json
config.vision (vision-span, vision-ocr): python/quantize_gptq_vision.py: GPTQ INT4, asymmetric groups of 32 with fp16 scales, as MatMulNBits, Hessians from 48 generated inputs per bundle; the image encoder and the text backbone with its token table are two shared files (backbone/vision/q4/image.onnx.data, text.onnx.data); each bundle keeps its own connector, LoRA (INT8 per channel) and heads; export report reports/quantization-gptq-vision.json

runtimes.text: Node.js CPU and WebGPU, Bun CPU, Chromium WASM and WebGPU, WebKit WebGPU (2026-11-08)
runtimes.vision: Node.js CPU and WebGPU, Bun CPU, Chromium WASM and WebGPU, WebKit WebGPU (2026-11-09)

tried: g8 fixes decode but span score drift 0.0216 > 0.02

rejected.reason: GPTQ g32 with the shared backbone: the noul fixture flips (FP32 p(yes) 0.563 to about 0.44); 3 of 177 held-out decisions flip, the 56 labelled cases stay 52 correct as with FP32; restoring any one layer or matrix type to FP32 removes at most 13% of the drift (reports/quantization-decision-sensitivity.json)
rejected.publishedBy: published since 2026-11-10 by python/verify_decision.py: 26 of 1,300 BoolQ answers differ from FP32, 1,103 correct for both (reports/quantization-decision.json)

rejected.reason: box point is an argmax over image cells sitting on a knife edge: task-graph quantization at any tested setting (Q8 per-channel/g64/g32/g8, Q4 g64/g32/g16) moves the point one cell (x 0.28125 -> 0.34375); Q4-g8 task-only passes the fixture by rounding luck and is not trusted; encoder-only Q4 (g16/g8) fails the gate too
tried: GPTQ g32 on both graphs (python/quantize_gptq_vision.py, 2026-11-09): the point moves from x 0.28125, y 0.28125 to x 0.71875, y 0.34375
rejected.publishedBy: published since 2026-11-12 by the accuracy gate scripts/verify-accuracy.ts: the point lies in the labelled region for 1,054 of 1,500 RefCOCO expressions against 1,062 for FP32 (reports/quantization-accuracy.json)

rejected.reason: task-graph Q8 alone (any grouping) flips the point argmax; accepted variant quantizes only the vision encoder

note: Fixture gates are necessary but not an accuracy benchmark; knife-edge fixture cases (ner unicode, vision-box point) dominate the rejections. The q4 bundles of ner, vision-box and decision/fast fail this gate and are published by an accuracy gate on a labelled set instead (publishedBy). FP32 remains the reference; every task loads q4 by default, q8 or FP32 on request.
